drivers.lead: Ogier equalled Loeb's nine at Rally Saudi Arabia in 2025, thirteen years after Loeb set the mark
drivers.note: Sébastien Loeb's nine were consecutive, 2004 to 2012 — nine seasons in which he never lost a championship. Sébastien Ogier's are spread over thirteen years and three teams: four with Volkswagen from 2013, two with M-Sport Ford in 2017 and 2018, and three with Toyota. The ninth is the strange one. He took it as a part-time driver, sitting out Sweden, Kenya and Estonia, starting eleven of the fourteen rounds and winning six of them, and he went into the final day two points ahead of his own team-mate Elfyn Evans. That is what makes this record hard to predict rather than hard to beat: Ogier is the only person who can extend it, and he is doing it without committing to a full season. Behind the two of them it thins out fast — Juha Kankkunen and Tommi Mäkinen have four each, and Kalle Rovanperä, the youngest champion the championship has had, left rallying after 2025 for single-seaters.

teams.lead: Counted from 1979, Toyota leads on nine, the fifth of its current run settled with two rounds to spare in 2025
teams.note: The scope matters on this one. The WRC has awarded a manufacturers' championship since 1973 but a drivers' championship only since 1979, and these records begin in 1979 — so Lancia's first three titles, won with the Stratos in 1974, 1975 and 1976, sit outside the count. Add them back and Lancia has ten, which is still the all-time record; Toyota's own account of its 2025 title placed the marque one short of it. Inside the window Lancia has seven: 1983, then six straight from 1987 to 1992. Toyota's nine are split by an eighteen-year absence from the championship — 1993, 1994 and 1999, then nothing until it returned and won in 2018 and every season from 2021. Citroën is third on eight, every one of them between 2003 and 2012, and it closed its works team at the end of 2019.
